title: Amber Extraction Lab
description: The user plays as a paleontologist in a lab examining a mosquito preserved in amber displayed behind a glass window case. They must adjust material properties of the amber (transparency, roughness, refraction) to analyze the specimen, then shatter the glass case to extract it, observing how material properties change under different lighting conditions.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive Amber Extraction Lab scene. Load both GLB assets: MosquitoInAmber.glb placed at center on a pedestal, and GlassBrokenWindow.glb positioned as a protective glass case surrounding the amber specimen (initially showing the unbroken state, scaled and positioned to enclose the amber). Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0, 1.5, 3.5) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to prevent going below the floor. Lighting: one warm DirectionalLight from upper-right, one cool-toned RimLight from behind, and a soft AmbientLight. Add an HDR-style environment using PMREMGenerator with a simple procedural gradient for reflections. Interaction steps: (1) User clicks a UI button labeled 'Analyze Amber' which animates the amber material's opacity from 1.0 down to 0.6 over 1 second, revealing internal detail, and sets transmission to 0.5 with ior of 1.55 using MeshPhysicalMaterial. (2) A 'Roughness' slider (range 0-1) appears allowing the user to adjust the amber surface roughness in real-time, visually changing from polished to matte. (3) A 'Lighting Mode' toggle switches between warm (3200K) and cool (6500K) color temperatures on the directional light so the user can compare how amber refracts under different conditions. (4) User clicks an 'Extract Specimen' button which triggers a shatter animation: the unbroken glass case fades out and the GlassBrokenWindow model fades in at the same position over 0.5 seconds with fragments slightly displaced outward using a short positional animation on child meshes. (5) After extraction, the amber floats upward with a gentle sine-wave hover animation and a spotlight focuses on it from above. Apply MeshPhysicalMaterial with clearcoat 1.0 and clearcoatRoughness 0.1 to the glass models. Add a dark wooden floor plane with MeshStandardMaterial. Include an HTML overlay panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background) for all UI controls styled cleanly. All models should cast and receive shadows with PCFSoftShadowMap enabled on the renderer.
